insights.speaker: Morten Springborg

insights.speaker: Morten Springborg

summary: C Worldwide strategist Morten Springborg discusses the geopolitical shift from a unipolar to multipolar world, comparing 2025 to 1989 in historical significance. Key investment themes include European defense rebuild (favoring Saab and Rheinmetall), quality capital goods companies, electrification, and a significant underweight to US equities which he considers at bubble levels. He advocates for global ex-US exposure, particularly in Europe and emerging markets, while expecting the dollar to depreciate against Asian currencies.
key_takeaways: 2025 marks a historic shift to a multipolar world - as significant as the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989
European defense companies Saab and Rheinmetall are favored due to strong domestic government finances; Southern European defense stocks like Leonardo face headwinds
US equity market at 70% of global markets is considered a bubble that will normalize to around 50% over 5-10 years
Europe desperately needs to rebuild manufacturing capacity and defense infrastructure - this creates massive investment opportunities
Quality capital goods companies and electrification themes are favored investment areas, particularly in Europe
Gold is rising as central banks build reserves for a new multipolar monetary system where gold serves as neutral reserve asset
China has structural advantages: only 13% energy import dependence vs Europe's 58%, and practical AI focus on automation vs Western pursuit of AGI
International ex-US strategy recommended as the place to be for long-term investors over next 10 years
